papers.title: $7$-adic Galois representations of elliptic curves over the rationals via Kummer descent
papers.summary: We show that the two modular curves of level $49$ and genus $9$ left open by the work of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and of Furio and Lombardo, have no non-CM rational points. Together with the theorem of Furio and Lombardo on $X_{ns}^{+}(49)$, this completes the classification of the $7$-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $Q$. The proof is a Kummer descent on the superelliptic equations $F(x,y) = k\,w^{7}$ of Furio and Lombardo, in the cases $7 \mid k$ that they left open. The covering curves are twists of the Fermat septic, they map to twists of the Klein quartic, and a $7$-adic computation shows that the twist attached to a solution is trivial. The rational points of the Klein quartic were determined by Hurwitz, who reduced the question to Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent $7$, proved by Lamé. Thus, the last open case of the $7$-adic part of Mazur's Program B rests on Fermat's Last Theorem for exponent $7$.

papers.title: Semisimplicity, purity and Mumford-Tate conjecture for hyper-Kähler varieties
papers.summary: We prove the Mumford-Tate conjecture in every degree for hyper-Kähler varieties over fields finitely generated over $\mathbb{Q}$. The proof establishes semisimplicity of $\ell$-adic cohomology by eliminating the unipotent radical of the algebraic monodromy group of total cohomology. We also prove the weight-monodromy conjecture for hyper-Kähler varieties over $p$-adic fields. For hyper-Kähler varieties over number fields with $b_2\geq 4$, we establish, after suitable finite extensions, strong compatibility of the associated Weil-Deligne representations valued in Mumford-Tate groups and its integral refinement away from finitely many primes.

papers.title: Derived supergeometry and perfect obstruction theories on algebraic superstacks
papers.summary: We develop a deformation-theoretic framework for algebraic superstacks and apply it to the construction of perfect obstruction theories on moduli spaces of stable supermaps. In order to achieve this we employ the tools and concepts from derived algebraic geometry, extending them to the supergeometric setting. Our main technical contributions are (i) the notions of derived superstacks, (ii) their cotangent supercomplexes and (iii) perfect obstruction theories for algebraic superstacks. We prove that a quasi-smooth derived enhancement of an algebraic superstack always yields a perfect obstruction theory: this generalizes a well-known principle from classical deformation theory. We then turn to the case of the Deligne--Mumford superstack $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathsf{st-}\mathrm{SUSY}}_{g,\mathfrak{n}}(\boldsymbol{Y})$ of stable supermaps of fixed genus, homology class and numbers of Neveu--Schwarz and Ramond--Ramond punctures, with target a smooth projective superscheme $\boldsymbol{Y}$. We exhibit a natural derived enhancement $\mathbb{R} \boldsymbol{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathsf{st-}\mathrm{SUSY}}_{g,\mathfrak{n}}(\boldsymbol{Y})$ and compute its cotangent supercomplex; we prove that the induced obstruction theory on $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathsf{st-}\mathrm{SUSY}}_{g,\mathfrak{n}}(\boldsymbol{Y})$ is perfect. Finally, we compute its virtual dimension by super Grothendieck--Riemann--Roch. The resulting formula gives, in particular, a deformation-theoretic proof of the virtual dimension formula previously conjectured for stable supermaps and specializes to the usual virtual dimension of the classical moduli stack of stable maps.

papers.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
papers.summary: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $Σ$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,Φ)$ with $(E,Φ)\cong(E,-Φ)$. For a complex reductive group $G$ realized as a self-adjoint subgroup of $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$, we show that if $(E,Φ)$ corresponds to a representation $ρ$ of $π_1(Σ)$, then $(E,-Φ)$ corresponds to $(\overlineρ^{\,t})^{-1}$. As a consequence, the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles is the fixed locus of an involution of the character variety and carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. For a connected semisimple group and every topological type, we prove that the reversible locus in the smooth moduli space is a $(B,A,A)$-brane. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $η\mapsto-η$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.

papers.summary: In this note, for every topological colored nonsymmetric operad with CW spaces in each arity we construct a homotopy isomorphism with a CW homotopy operad (i.e. all higher homotopies are cellular with respect to the product structure and CW structure on cubes) not changing its objects. By using the two-sided bar construction, we rectify this to a homotopy isomorphism with a strict CW operad. This applies more generally to topological algebras over colored operads in sets. In the case of diagrams of finite CW complexes over finite posets, the resulting diagram consists of finite CW spaces enhancing the Quillen adjunction between simplicial sets and topological spaces. As a byproduct, we produce an embedding of topological homotopy algebras over operads into the presheaf category over the branch resolution for the category of $P$-trees generalizing the known case of topological operads.

papers.title: Generalized Thom Spectra, Conjugate Stacks, and truncated Brown-Peterson Spectra
papers.summary: We propose a of definition conjugate stack for a class of suitable $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-algebras that includes the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle$ for all heights $n$. Then we calculate part of $\mathrm{BP}\langle n \rangle^{\mathrm{conj}}$ as a quotient stack in terms of Witt vectors. To perform this computation we study generalized Thom spectra and their relative Topological Hochschild Homology. We exhibit the Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectrum $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{F}_2$ as a $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectrum, the $p$-local Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/p^n$ (except for $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}/4$) and $\mathrm{H}\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ as $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}_{(p)}$-Thom spectra, and the connective complex K-theory spectrum $ku$ as $\mathbb{E}_1$-$\mathrm{MU}$-Thom spectra. We accompany these ``go" results with ``no-go" results that show these ``go" results do not admit $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-refinements.

papers.title: Cohen-Lenstra heuristics and vanishing of zeta functions for superelliptic curves over finite fields
papers.summary: We prove a Cohen-Lenstra type result commenting on the distribution of class group structures amongst function fields of superelliptic curves over finite fields. We also prove a result commenting on the sparsity of such superelliptic curves whose zeta functions vanish at a fixed complex number. These results are proven via point-counting techniques on certain Hurwitz schemes generalizing techniques of Ellenberg-Venkatesh-Westerland and Ellenberg-Li-Shusterman. To obtain these point counts, We prove a unitary big monodromy theorem generalizing big monodromy theorems of Yu and Achter-Pries by appealing to an arithmeticity theorem of Venkataramana.

papers.title: $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectedness of moduli of semistable bundles and symplectic bundles on a curve
papers.summary: In this note, we show that over a geometrically irreducible smooth projective curve over an infinite field $k$, the moduli stack of semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected if and only if the moduli stack admits a $k$-rational point. For this we use Langton's elementary modifications for vector bundles at the level of families. In addition, we prove the $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectedness of the moduli stack of symplectic bundles with forms valued in a fixed line bundle $L$ on a smooth projective curve of genus $g \ge 2$ over an infinite field $k$ with $C(k)\neq \emptyset$. As an application, we deduce the $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectedness of moduli stack of quasi-parabolic symplectic vector bundles with forms valued in a fixed line bundle.

papers.title: $\ell$-Independence, slopes, and weights of $\ell$-adic cohomology groups of rigid spaces
papers.summary: Let $\ell$ and $p$ be distinct prime numbers, $K$ a local field with residue characteristic $p$, $C$ a complete algebraically closed extension of $K$, and $X$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid space over $K$. When $\mathop{\mathrm{char}} K = 0$, we prove that the alternating sum of traces of elements in the positive part of the Weil group acting on $RΓ(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$ is independent of $\ell$ and is an integer, extending a result of Mieda to the singular case. We also give optimal bounds for the $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius liftings acting on $H^i(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$, proving a conjecture of Lu--Zheng. In the general case, we give optimal bounds for the $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius liftings acting on $H^i_c(X_C,\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})$, and we show that these eigenvalues are algebraic integers and Weil numbers, thereby extending results of Lu--Zheng and Mieda to the positive characteristic case.

papers.title: Loyalty of the affine line in motivic homotopy theory
papers.summary: We show that integers act invertibly on a derived scheme $S$ if and only if they act invertibly on the reduced motivic suspension spectrum of the affine line in $\mathrm{MS}_S$. As a consequence, over regular locally noetherian schemes and derived schemes on which some nonzero integer acts as zero, the motivic sphere spectrum is $\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant after inverting primes that are not invertible in the base scheme. In particular, over regular locally noetherian $\mathbf{Q}$-schemes, the motivic sphere spectrum is $\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant.

papers.title: Aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera of Kähler varieties
papers.summary: We study several aspects of deformation invariance of plurigenera in Kähler families over a smooth curve. First, for a relatively flat coherent sheaf, we characterize local constancy of fiberwise cohomology dimension by equivalent conditions in terms of extension, base change, torsion freeness of higher direct images, and the vanishing of jumping classes. Then, combining this criterion with the Kähler minimal model program, we prove invariance of plurigenera for Kähler families of threefolds whose central fiber has canonical singularities, and for smooth Kähler families of maximal Albanese dimension. We also establish deformation invariance of log plurigenera when the central fiber is projective, and is of log general type. We prove the invariance of higher cohomological plurigenera assuming that the canonical bundle of the total space is semipositive. Finally, we extend Z.~Li--Z.~Wang's deformation invariance result for generalized polarized pairs with abundant nef parts from projective families to Moishezon families.

papers.title: Cominuscule Richardson varieties
papers.summary: A Richardson variety in a cominuscule flag variety is defined by a skew shape of boxes. We prove that any cominuscule Richardson variety has a unique decomposition as a product of indecomposable cominuscule Richardson varieties, which are given by the connected components of the skew shape. We also prove that the first Chow group and the Picard group of a cominuscule Richardson variety are dual to each other; both are free abelian groups of rank equal to the number of indecomposable factors. Along the way, we construct an explicit desingularization of any cominuscule Richardson variety of classical Lie type as a tower of (isotropic) Grassmannian bundles. Our results imply that the Hilbert polynomial of the minimal ample line bundle is a well-defined geometric invariant of any cominuscule Richardson variety. We give a positive formula for this Hilbert polynomial.

papers.title: Indexed Logarithmic Cartier Transform
papers.summary: This article is the third of a series of three articles whose goal is to generalize the Cartier transform of Ogus and Vologodsky to the logarithmic setting. In the second one, we generalized a topos-theoretic version of this transform, due to Oyama. Let $W$ be the ring of Witt vectors of a perfect field of positive characteristic $p$ and equip $\operatorname{Spf}W$ with the trivial log structure. Let $\mathfrak{S}$ be an fs log $p$-adic formal scheme, locally of finite type and log flat over $\operatorname{Spf}W$ and denote its special fiber by $S.$ For a log smooth morphism of logarithmic schemes $X \rightarrow S,$ we constructed crystalline-like ringed topoi $\mathcal{E}'$ and $\underline{\mathcal{E}}$ and subcategories of crystals of quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal{C}'$ and $\underline{\mathcal{C}},$ equivalent respectively, under some lifting assumption, to modules with Higgs fields and integrable connections, both satisfying certain nilpotence conditions, and a morphism of topoi $\underline{\mathcal{E}} \rightarrow \mathcal{E}'.$ We proved that the pullback functor of this morphism of topoi preserves quasi-coherent crystals and induces a fully faithful functor $\mathcal{C}' \rightarrow \underline{\mathcal{C}}.$ Since the Frobenius morphism is not, in general, flat in the log smooth setting, it is not clear that this functor is essentially surjective. To address this issue, we refine the topoi and crystals mentioned above by endowing them with an indexed structure, inspired by Lorenzon's indexed extension of Cartier descent to smooth logarithmic schemes. Using the Azumaya property of the indexed algebra of logarithmic differential operators, we then obtain an equivalence between the corresponding categories of indexed crystals, thereby generalizing the Cartier transform.

papers.title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
papers.summary: We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously. The proofs of these inequalities follow a common three-step pattern: from microscopic local estimates to local estimates, and then to global estimates. Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Bundles on Cluster Varieties
papers.summary: We study algebraic vector bundles on cluster varieties. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, every algebraic vector bundle is trivial on a cluster variety with principal coefficients at an acyclic seed of irreducible finite Dynkin type. The proof is based on integral contractions of cellular $\mathbb A^1$-chain complexes and successive freezing. We also construct smooth cluster varieties admitting indecomposable rank-two vector bundles, whose nontriviality is detected by quadratic Euler classes. The cellular calculation also gives a criterion for stable freeness and computes integral real cohomology and the images of cycle class maps.

papers.title: New algebraic points on covers of elliptic curves
papers.summary: For a smooth projective curve $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus $\geq 2$ and $L/\mathbb{Q}$ an extension, we write $C(L)_{\text{new}}=\{P\in C(L):\mathbb{Q}(P)=L\}$. Recent work of Khawaja and Siksek conjectures that this set is empty for $100\%$ of degree $n$ number fields $L$, when ordered by absolute discriminant. Moreover, they bring evidence towards this conjecture when $C$ is a degree $n$ cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$. We complement their work by proving analogous results for degree $n$ covers $ψ:C\to E$ of elliptic curves $E$. Our main result shows that, under suitable hypotheses, the number of distinct absolute discriminants at most $X$ of primitive degree $n$ fields $L$ with $C(L)_{\text{new}}\neq\varnothing$ is $O(X^{1/2})$ or $O(X/(\log X)^α)$, for some $α>0$. In degrees $2,3,4$ and $5$ we show that these fields have density $0$ among all fields of the same degree (in degree $4$, also among the primitive ones). The novelty is for degrees $4$ and $5$, where we use work of Bhargava--Shankar--Wang and McGown--Thorne--Tucker to count fields with specified local constraints. Moreover, we give concrete examples of $8$ bielliptic modular curves $X_0(N)$, for which $X_0(N)(L)_{\text{new}}=\emptyset$ for $100 \%$ of quadratic fields $L$. Lastly, we point out modular covers of degrees $3$ and $5$ in the LMFDB for which similar conclusions hold.

papers.title: A Bogomolov property for moduli spaces of polynomials over abelian extensions
papers.summary: Let $d\geq2$ be an integer, and let $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ be the moduli space of degree-$d$ polynomials. For every number field $K$, we prove that there exists $ε_{K,d}>0$ such that \[ \left\lbraceα\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(α)<ε_{K,d}\right\rbrace=\left\lbraceα\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(α)=0\right\rbrace \] is finite, where $h_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the critical height. In particular, only finitely many $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$-rational points of $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ are postcritically finite. The proof combines the correspondence method of Ji--Song--Xie with local ramification estimates and the uniform finiteness of intertwined classes in $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$. We also prove an analogous finiteness theorem for non-preperiodic marked points in non-isotrivial one-parameter polynomial families.

papers.title: Elliptic curves attached to Jacobians with imaginary multiplication
papers.summary: Let M be an imaginary quadratic field and A be an abelian variety of odd dimension g defined over Q for which there is a unitary algebra embedding of M in End^0(A_M) of signature ((g+1)/2,(g-1)/2). Extending a result by Fité and Goodman, we show the existence of an elliptic curve E over Q with complex multiplication by M such that H_et^1(E_Qbar, Q_l) is a G_Q-subrepresentation of H_et^g ( A_Qbar, Q_l((g-1)/2) ). The main results of the article consist on explicit descriptions of E for A in two different families. First, when A is the Jacobian of the curve y^2 = xh(x^2), where h in Z[x] is a degree g monic separable polynomial with nonzero h(0), we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + h(0)x. Second, when A is the Jacobian of y^3=f(x), where h in Z[x] is a degree 4 monic separable polynomial, we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + 16 disc(f). This latter result builds on work by Laga and Shnidman in the bielliptic case, of which we give an alternative proof by means of a new p-adic method. As an application, we derive a practical average polynomial time algorithm to compute the Zeta functions of the reductions of a Picard curve.

papers.fulltext_excerpt: [2610.19069] Elliptic curves attached to Jacobians with imaginary multiplication Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Mathematics > Number Theory arXiv:2610.19069 (math) [Submitted on 13 Oct 2026] Title: Elliptic curves attached to Jacobians with imaginary multiplication Authors: Francesc Fité , Francesc Pedret View a PDF of the paper titled Elliptic curves attached to Jacobians with imaginary multiplication, by Francesc Fit\'e and Francesc Pedret View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Let M be an imaginary quadratic field and A be an abelian variety of odd dimension g defined over Q for which there is a unitary algebra embedding of M in End^0(A_M) of signature ((g+1)/2,(g-1)/2). Extending a result by Fité and Goodman, we show the existence of an elliptic curve E over Q with complex multiplication by M such that H_et^1(E_Qbar, Q_l) is a G_Q-subrepresentation of H_et^g ( A_Qbar, Q_l((g-1)/2) ). The main results of the article consist on explicit descriptions of E for A in two different families. First, when A is the Jacobian of the curve y^2 = xh(x^2), where h in Z[x] is a degree g monic separable polynomial with nonzero h(0), we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + h(0)x. Second, when A is the Jacobian of y^3=f(x), where h in Z[x] is a degree 4 monic separable polynomial, we show that E is given by y^2 = x^3 + 16 disc(f). This latter result builds on work by Laga and Shnidman in the bielliptic case, of which we give an alternative proof by means of a new p-adic method. As an application, we derive a practical average polynomial time algorithm to compute the Zeta functions of the reductions of a Picard curve. papers.title: A Bogomolov property for moduli spaces of polynomials over abelian extensions
papers.summary: Let $d\geq2$ be an integer, and let $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ be the moduli space of degree-$d$ polynomials. For every number field $K$, we prove that there exists $ε_{K,d}>0$ such that \[ \left\lbraceα\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(α)<ε_{K,d}\right\rbrace=\left\lbraceα\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(α)=0\right\rbrace \] is finite, where $h_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the critical height. In particular, only finitely many $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$-rational points of $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ are postcritically finite. The proof uses a universal critical-divisor family, a nef adelic line bundle with an explicit orbit-height formula, the intertwined relation, local ramification estimates, and the correspondence method of Ji--Song--Xie.

papers.title: Geometric families of multiple elliptic Gamma functions and arithmetic applications, III
papers.summary: This is the third paper in a series where we study arithmetic applications of the higher elliptic Gamma functions. In the first two articles in this series, we defined geometric families of these functions and proved that they satisfy coboundary and cocycle relations under the action of special linear groups and associated congruence subgroups. The main purpose of the present paper is to present a construction of conjectural higher elliptic units above number fields with exactly one complex place as special values of higher elliptic Gamma functions, upgrading the construction carried out by Bergeron, Charollois and García for complex cubic fields. These higher elliptic units are obtained by evaluating a multiplicative $(n-2)$-cocycle built from higher elliptic Gamma functions against a $(n-2)$-cycle associated to some group of totally positive units of a given number field of degree $n$ with exactly one complex place. We conjecture that these higher elliptic units are algebraic units which belong to prescribed abelian extensions of the base field where they are evaluated and that they satisfy a Kronecker limit formula which relates the logarithm of their modulus to values of derivatives of partial zeta functions at $s = 0$ in the base field. We showcase our conjecture on various examples for number fields of degree 3, 4 and 5.

papers.title: Chow groups of symmetric products of projective space
papers.summary: We prove that the integral cycle class map for $\SP^d(\PP^n)$ is split injective, with finite cokernel annihilated by $d!$,and we determine the ranks of Chow groups for $\mathrm{SP}^d(\mathbb{P}^n)$. Compatible integral transfer retractions show that $\CH_q(\SP^d(\PP^n))$ stabilizes for $d\geq q$. An explicit nonalgebraic order two class persists under addition of points, producing a split cokernel summand even in the range $q\leq d$ and in the infinite symmetric product. For the smooth configuration open set, we identify the codimension two cokernel with third unramified cohomology and detect its ramification on a rational resolution. In contrast to addition, even multiplicities annihilate a nonzero Chow class.

papers.title: Frobenius splitting of valuation rings revisited
papers.summary: Let $K$ be a function field over an $F$-finite field $k$ of characteristic $p > 0$ and let $ν$ be a valuation of $K/k$. We show $ν$ is an Abhyankar valuation of $K/k$ if and only if the corresponding valuation ring is Frobenius split. The proof proceeds by analyzing when ideals of a valuation ring are uniformly $F$-compatible and establishing a general ramification-theoretic characterization of Frobenius split valuation rings of $F$-finite fields. In addition, when the ground field $k$ is not $F$-finite, we show that the equivalence between Frobenius splitting and the Abhyankar property can fail by constructing an example of an excellent Frobenius split DVR of a function field whose corresponding valuation is not divisorial. Our methods do not rely on local uniformization results.

papers.title: Quillen's local parameter conjecture in dimension four
papers.summary: Let $R$ be a Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic and dimension four, and let $r$ be a member of a regular system of parameters. We prove that every finitely generated projective module over $R[1/r]$ is free. We also prove that $\mathrm{Sp}_4(R[1/r])$ acts transitively on unimodular columns of length four and that every determinant orientation of a rank-two projective module is induced by a basis. The argument reduces freeness to two vanishing results: the degree-three Zariski cohomology of the naive degree-four Milnor--Witt sheaf and the alternating Witt group of $R[1/r]$. We establish these results using integral degree-two algebraic $K$-theory, supported hermitian $K$-theory, and local motivic cohomology. A finite-rank symplectic comparison relates the image of the completion obstruction to Milnor--Witt multiplication and yields the required symplectic frames.

papers.title: Geometry of a semistable degeneration of moduli of vector bundles on curves
papers.summary: We study the Gieseker moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{X_0}$ of stable rank-$2$, degree-$1$ vector bundles on an irreducible curve $X_0$ with one node. Its normalization is a two-step blow-up of the moduli space of generalized parabolic bundles on the normalization $\tilde X_0$, and $\mathcal{M}_{X_0}$ is recovered by gluing along a natural involution on the boundary. From this we compute $\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal{M}_{X_0})$ and, via a Harder--Narasimhan stratification, the virtual Poincaré polynomial of $\mathcal{M}_{X_0}$. Since the normalization morphism is small, the intersection cohomology of $\mathcal{M}_{X_0}$ equals the ordinary cohomology of the smooth normalization, which gives a closed formula in terms of the arithmetic genus.

papers.title: Generic Hodge and special Hodge--Witt polygons
papers.summary: We prove that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal O_C$ lies on or above the generalized Hodge--Witt polygon of its special fiber. The argument combines prismatic cohomology with Ekedahl's diagonal theory of coherent Raynaud complexes. For each integral cutoff and each finite iteration length, a finite iterated Nygaard construction produces a perfect $A_{\mathrm{inf}}$-complex. Its individual-degree lengths along the generic divisor branches are weighted Hodge sums. A maximal-minor specialization argument bounds their sum by the corresponding crystalline length. On the special fiber, an exact derived modification of coherent Raynaud complexes has length growth governed by weighted Hodge--Witt numbers, with bounded error. Passing to the limit in these numerical lengths gives the comparison, allowing negative Hodge--Witt numbers and crystalline torsion. No projectivity, algebraization, or descent to a discretely valued field is assumed.

papers.title: Nef Hattori classes and products of projective lines
papers.summary: Let \(X\) be a smooth connected complex projective variety with an effective algebraic \(\mathbb C^{\times}\)-action, a nonempty finite fixed locus whose weights are \(\pm1\). We show that if its Hattori line bundles are nef, then \(X\) is algebraically isomorphic to \((\mathbb{P}^1)^{\dim X}\), and these bundles become the hyperplane bundles of the factors. The product statement follows from the nef-complexity classification of Enwright and collaborators, and we describe the isomorphism through global sections. To test the required nefness we specialise the orbit-graph criterion of Romano and Wiśniewski. The Hirzebruch surface \(\mathbb F_2\) is an example why the topological hypotheses alone do not imply either the product conclusion or the Fano property.

papers.title: The local structure of refined class groups in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory
papers.summary: We give an explicit local description of ray class refinements in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory. For distinct primes $p\geq5$ and $\ell$, and even $2\leq k\leq p-3$, we prove that the $ω^{1-k}$-component of the $p$-primary ray class group of $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)$, with squarefree modulus supported above $\ell$, is nonzero if and only if $p\mid\ell(1-\ell^k)B_k$. In the cyclotomic tower, we determine the local modules and their correction modulo the diagonal global Tate module, obtaining an explicit determinant formula. Their Frobenius Euler factors, combined with the Mazur--Wiles theorem, yield a ray class form of the Iwasawa main conjecture for nonexceptional odd characters. We also obtain exact class number valuation comparisons at every layer, including those before stabilization, recover Finat's formula for $\ell=2$, and deduce refined $μ$-vanishing from Ferrero--Washington. The cyclotomic character explains the Wieferich exception, while existing Eisenstein congruence theorems connect the divisibility criteria with prime-level Ramanujan-style congruences.

papers.title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
papers.summary: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.

papers.title: K-Moduli Wall Crossing and Automorphic Forms for the Moduli Space of Rational Elliptic Surfaces
papers.summary: Using K-moduli spaces for log quasimaps $q_t\colon\left(\mathbb P^1,\frac{1-t}{12}D\right)\to[\mathbb A^2/\mathbb G_m]$ of degree twelve with twelve points and weight $t/12$, we construct a modular interpolation $\{\mathcal M_t\}_{0\le t\le1}$ between the Baily--Borel compactification of the Heckman--Looijenga ball quotient $X_o$ and Miranda's GIT compactification of the moduli space of rational elliptic surfaces. We completely determine the wall-crossing and, for every rational $t\in[0,1]$, identify \[ \mathcal M_t\cong\operatorname{Proj}R\!\left(X_o,\mathcal L+\frac t2Δ(6)+\frac t3Δ(9)\right), \] where $\mathcal L$ is the automorphic $\mathbb Q$-line bundle and $Δ(6),Δ(9)$ are distinguished Heegner divisors. On the automorphic side, we construct a new automorphic form on $X_o$ via a Borcherds product, whose divisor gives an independent relation among the Heegner divisors. This relation provides a key input for determining the birational transformations in the K-moduli wall-crossing. As part of this analysis, we show that the first positive chamber $\mathcal M_t$ for $t\in (0,1/7)$ is Looijenga's semi-toroidal compactification.

papers.title: The Kuranishi space of joint deformations of Calabi--Yau manifolds and holomorphic vector bundles
papers.summary: In this paper, we study joint deformations of pairs $(X,E)$, where $X$ is a compact complex manifold and $E\rightarrow X$ is a holomorphic vector bundle. We prove that $(X,E)$ has unobstructed deformations if $X$ is a Fujiki manifold with torsion canonical bundle and $H^2(X,\textrm{End}^0E)=0$, where $\textrm{End}^0 E$ denotes the trace-free endomorphism bundle. When the canonical bundle is trivial, the Fujiki assumption can be replaced by three weak $\partial\bar\partial$-conditions. We construct examples satisfying these conditions whose Frölicher spectral sequences do not degenerate at $E_1$. These results provide non-Kähler extensions of the theorems of Li--Pan and Iacono--Manetti. Without this vanishing assumption, we obtain both unobstructed and obstructed pairs. papers.title: Golod--Shafarevich for arithmetic surfaces
papers.summary: We construct Golod--Shafarevich towers of arithmetic surfaces over the integers. In particular, we obtain an arithmetic surface with a section and infinite geometric etale fundamental group, answering a question raised by Bost and Charles about the existence of such surfaces. Taking generic fibres gives curves over the rationals with infinite geometric etale towers in which a rational point splits completely. This answers questions posed by Ihara and by Frey, Kani and Völklein. Taking the generic fibres of the tower, we also obtain sequence of curves over the rationals whose genera goes to infinity and whose logarithmic conductors grows no more than linearly in the genera, answering a question asked by Venkatesh at PCMI in 2022. The authors worked together on this problem since 2022 and developed a general strategy. They were able to bring it to fruit only after a collaboration with GPT5.6 Sol, Fable and Aletheia a Gemini-powered internal agent developed at Google DeepMind.

papers.title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction
papers.summary: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.

papers.title: K-moduli wall crossing for quasimaps to a projective variety
papers.summary: We develop a modular wall crossing theory for quasimaps to a projective variety, allowing independent variation of the boundary coefficients and the quasimap weight. Building on the K-stability of quasimaps introduced by Hashizume and the first author, we construct projective moduli spaces in the stable, Calabi--Yau, and log Fano regimes, together with wall crossing morphisms. A central construction is the moduli theory of boundary polarized Calabi--Yau quasimaps, which retains an ample polarization at the numerically trivial locus and allows comparison with suitable perturbations toward the stable and log Fano regions. The stable theory applies in arbitrary genus, while the comparisons through the Calabi--Yau locus concern genus zero. For degree-one boundary divisors, the resulting framework relates weighted stable maps and quasimaps to Hassett spaces and GIT quotients of weighted points on $\mathbb P^1$. In a companion paper, we apply this framework to give a modular interpolation between Miranda's GIT compactification of rational elliptic surfaces and the Baily--Borel compactification of an eight-dimensional ball quotient.

papers.title: Hyperquiver varieties
papers.summary: We discuss the recently introduced concept of hyperquivers, due to Muller, Nanda, and Seigal, from the point of view of Kähler and hyperkähler quotients. In particular, we show that the Kähler hyperquiver variety ${\mathcal M}$, corresponding to a hyperquiver with a single hyperedge, is a projective variety isomorphic to the geometric quotient of the space of tensors with maximal multilinear rank. Moreover, the hyperkähler hyperquiver variety corresponding to doubling of this hyperquiver can be identified with the linear scheme corresponding to the sheaf of reflexive $1$-forms on ${\mathcal M}$.

papers.title: Degeneracy loci and unlikely intersections in abelian schemes
papers.summary: Let $\mathcal{A}\to S$ be an abelian scheme over a normal quasi-projective variety over a number field, and let $\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{A}$ be a positive-dimensional subvariety. For every integer $t>0$, we prove that, outside the $t$-degeneracy locus of $\mathcal{X}$, at most finitely many points lie in flat group subschemes of relative dimension less than $t$. In particular, this intersection is not Zariski dense whenever $\mathcal{X}$ is $t$-nondegenerate. The proof combines a bounded height theorem with uniform large Galois orbit estimates, o-minimal point counting, and mixed Ax--Schanuel, following the Pila--Zannier strategy. The arithmetic input is an explicit bound for the complexity of endomorphism relations, obtained from geometry of numbers and height estimates for abelian varieties. As applications, we formulate a relative Mordell--Lang conjecture, prove it for section images in powers of certain abelian schemes, and establish injectivity of specialization of the group of sections outside a proper closed subset under variation and dimension hypotheses.

papers.title: Simpson filtrations and closure relations of Hodge moduli spaces
papers.summary: In this paper, we study closure relations of Simpson strata in Hodge moduli spaces over a smooth complex projective curve of genus $g\geq2$ and prove in every rank that the Heinloth weight strictly increases whenever a specialization changes the fixed component. For stable full chains, we refine this numerical condition by comparing the degrees of the corresponding filtration steps and construct counterexamples to Simpson's nestedness conjecture for the Dolbeault and de Rham moduli spaces in every rank $n\geq4$. Using the maximum property of this weight, we also discuss Simpson filtrations from the viewpoint of $Θ$ stratifications.

papers.title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields
papers.summary: We prove that every number field of degree $n$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has a defining integral polynomial of degree $n$ whose coefficients are all $O_n(\sqrt D)$ in size, thus resolving a 1998 conjecture of Ruppert. Our proof compares ideal lattices with their trace duals, via which we handle all number fields with the exception of CM fields whose maximal totally real subfields have small discriminant. We then treat the remaining fields by averaging completed Epstein zeta functions over all possible ideal classes and archimedean scalings, for which we make critical use of Hecke's formula and the subconvexity theorem of Michel and~Venkatesh. Our proof does not use the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis.

papers.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
papers.summary: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.

papers.title: The logarithmic generalised Kummer locus and its tropicalisation
papers.summary: We construct a separated logarithmic compactification of a divisor in the moduli of polarised irreducible holomorphic symplectic (IHS) varieties of generalised Kummer type in dimension at least four. This compactification carries a universal family of logarithmic IHS varieties, and its tropicalisation carries a universal family of tropical generalised Kummer varieties. The compactification is built from a more general construction of explicit, projective, and logarithmically smooth models for type~II and type~III degenerations of generalised Kummer varieties of arbitrary dimension and over base logarithmic schemes of any dimension. Over a base of any logarithmic rank, these degenerations come with a tropicalisation map to a family of integral affine manifolds with singularities, and with boundary in the type II case. This tropical family is constructed through a tropical generalised Kummer construction. Our approach uses logarithmic Hilbert schemes to extend the conventional generalised Kummer construction to families of logarithmic abelian varieties. We describe fibres of our degenerations, and thus every point in the boundary of our compactification. Proper models correspond to polyhedral structures on the associated tropical generalised Kummer variety, with the resulting polyhedral complex serving as the dual intersection complex; each irreducible component is constructed by applying the generalised Kummer construction to a product of logarithmic group compactifications of semi-abelian varieties.

papers.title: Some applications of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis to class groups and small generators of number fields
papers.summary: We prove an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem, conditional on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function. Drawing on recent breakthroughs of OpenAI and Cureton--Thorner, we make unconditional the Ellenberg--Venkatesh bounds on $\ell$-torsion in class groups of number fields and extend an averaged result of Lemke Oliver--Smith to arbitrary families of degree-$d$-fields. Further applications are given to the least prime splitting and to small generators in number fields.

papers.title: The classical homotopy category is cartesian closed
papers.summary: The category of all topological spaces and homotopy classes of maps is cartesian closed. In fact, the $(\infty, 1)$-category of all topological spaces and continuous maps, localised at homotopy equivalences, is cartesian closed. We model the exponential object using a topological space whose points are continuous maps equipped with putative neighbourhood filters. In general, this topological space will not even be $T_1$-separated, but the evaluation map induces a natural weak homotopy equivalence witnessing the universal property.

papers.title: On the conjectural Hodge index theorem for finite quotient spaces of singular varieties
papers.summary: We study the conjectural characteristic class analogue of the Hodge index theorem for singular complex algebraic varieties, formulated by Brasselet-Schürmann-Yokura which expresses the Goresky-MacPherson homology $L$-classes in terms of suitable Hodge-theoretic $L$-classes, for quotient spaces $X/G$, where $G$ is a finite group and $X$ is a pure-dimensional complex projective variety. Assuming that an equivariant $K$-theoretical version of the conjecture holds for $X$, we show that the characteristic class conjecture holds for $X/G$. Without assuming the equivariant $K$-theoretical version, we show that the characteristic class conjecture holds for $X/G$, provided that it holds for all fixed point sets $X^g$ and that a suitable normally nonsingular inclusion assumption is satisfied. Our approach is to work in equivariant analytic $K$-homology and equivariant algebraic $G$-theory and to identify the corresponding localized classes. On the analytic side, we identify the Banagl-Zagier equivariant $L$-classes with localized Chern character of the equivariant $K$-homology class of the signature operator defined by Banagl-Leichtnam-Piazza. On the algebraic side, we compute the localization of the equivariant motivic Hodge-Chern class transformation of the intersection Hodge module.

papers.title: Universal norms of partially de Rham $B$-pairs and perfectness in Lubin--Tate Iwasawa theory
papers.summary: We study the behaviour of partially de Rham Selmer groups of $B$-pairs along abelian $p$-adic Lie extensions. In the cyclotomic case we compare them with the universal norms studied by Berger. For analytic Lubin--Tate $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules we prove that the $Ψ=1$ eigenspace is coadmissible of the expected rank over the algebra of analytic distributions and establish a comparison result between its Lie-algebra coinvariants and the projective limit of the partially de Rham Selmer groups of the attached $B$-pair.

papers.title: The unbearable projectivity of being a good moduli space of Gorenstein curves of genus one with non-colliding markings
papers.summary: We classify all open substacks admitting a proper good moduli space inside the stack $\mathcal{G}_{1,n}$ of log-canonically polarized Gorenstein curves of genus one with $n$ distinct marked points: they are exactly the stacks $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{1,n}(c)$ defined by Bozlee--Kuo--Neff. papers.title: $G$-Equivariant Hilbert Schemes and Quadratic Forms
papers.summary: For a finite abelian group $G$ acting linearly on the plane let $\mathcal{X}$ be the associated quotient stack. We analyze a fine moduli space which parameterizes zero dimensional substacks of $\mathcal{X}$ whose corresponding subschemes of the plane have a given representation type, denoted by $\mathcal{X}^{[ρ]}$. By means of a Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem of Toën we give explicit representation theoretic formulas of $\dim(\mathcal{X}^{[ρ]})$ for all $ρ\in \operatorname{Rep}(G)$ which are similar to the McKay correspondence. We also give a classification of all such quotient stacks according to an associated quadratic form called the Euler form. papers.title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
papers.summary: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonné theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the étale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.

papers.title: Mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes
papers.summary: This work studies the relationship between the multigrading in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes, introduced by V. Buchstaber and T. Panov in their computation of these cohomology groups, and the multigrading in the cohomology of the corresponding complements of coordinate subspace arrangements, arising from the mixed Hodge structure. It is shown that these multigradings coincide. This result refines a theorem from Yu. Eliyashev's 2013 dissertation. Furthermore, results on the mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of complements of coordinate subspace arrangements are applied to the study of the same varieties over finite fields. In particular, various formulas are obtained for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and for the associated global $ζ$-functions.

papers.title: Braidings of Self-Equivalences and Bordism
papers.summary: Let $M$ be a closed, smooth or topological $n$-manifold, with $n \geq 4$. We construct a homotopy highly cartesian square relating the space ${\mathcal E}(M (\ell))$ of homotopy self-equivalences of $M$ (in a suitable range) over the Postnikov $\ell$-sections of its stable normal microbundle, and an $(\infty + n)$-fold loop space representing an associated (normal) bordism theory. This implies the existence of braids of interlocking exact sequences involving the homotopy groups of ${\mathcal E}(M(\ell))$ and certain Lashof bordism groups, leading to a conceptual explanation and broad generalization of earlier work of Hambleton--Kreck for closed, oriented $4$-manifolds.

papers.title: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
papers.summary: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients. Furthermore, some embedding problems of orders can be studied via quotient graphs. These results provide a geometric framework for the study of maximal orders over function fields. In this article, we extend that construction to a higher dimensional setting through the use of singular chain complexes. Then we describe the set of vertices in this quotient that correspond to split maximal orders and the topology of the corresponding region of the quotient complex. More precisely, we show that these ``split vertices'' fall into a finite number of quotients of apartments by suitable subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group, the symmetric group. We relate these ``quotient apartments'' with the cuspidal sectors defined by previous authors who studied the quotient by the group of integral points of the special linear group. Both quotients are indeed related by a ramified cover that is unramified on cusps, as proved here.

papers.title: On Igusa's conjectures for weighted homogeneous polynomials with isolated singularities
papers.summary: In 1991, Denef introduced an explicit formula for Igusa's local zeta functions in terms of embedded resolutions of singularities over $p$-adic fields with good reduction. In this paper, by slightly generalizing the $p$-adic McKay correspondence given by the second author in 2017, we extend Denef's result to the setting of $\mathbb{Q}$-embedded resolutions of singularities. Consequently, the strong monodromy conjecture with respect to Igusa's local zeta functions holds for weighted homogeneous polynomials with isolated singularities. Moreover, we use our formula to prove Igusa's conjecture for exponential sums in the case of non-degenerate weighted homogeneous polynomials with isolated singularities.

papers.title: Topological realizations of finite posets
papers.summary: I introduce a new class of cell complexes, called CL-complexes, that provide alternative topological realizations of finite posets. Each realization of a given poset has the same homotopy type as the order complex of that, so in some sense these spaces do not provide anything really new. Their value is that they enable short transparent proofs of standard results in poset homotopy. These include Quillen's Theorem A for finite posets, the Nerve Theorem for good covers of a topological space, and Sheehy's multicover generalization of the Nerve Theorem. Order complexes retain a special status: the order complex of a finite poset admits CL-complex structures both for the poset itself and for its opposite poset. The definition of CL-complexes is motivated by an elementary generalization of the Carrier Lemma of J. W. Walker, which in its original form constructs a canonical homotopy class of maps from a simplicial complex to a space covered by a suitable family of contractible sets. In the generalized lemma, the role played by simplicial complexes and the role played by spaces covered by contractible sets can both be fulfilled by CL-complexes. This sets up an equivalence of categories that tacitly underlies our approach.

papers.title: Appell Sequences in Analytic Number Theory: Shifted Expansions and Dirichlet L-Functions
papers.summary: We place the Appell shift theorem for asymptotic expansions inside a Borel--Laplace framework and apply it to two classical functions of analytic number theory: the Hurwitz zeta function \(ζ(m,q)\) and the Lerch transcendent \(Φ(z,m,a)\). The resulting shifted expansions have coefficients given by Appell polynomials evaluated at the shift, with remainders controlled uniformly on compact sets. The generating sequences are identified explicitly in terms of the Taylor coefficients of the Borel kernels. In a second direction, we extend the Appell--Mellin framework of Navas, Ruiz and Varona to Dirichlet \(L\)-functions. For a primitive non-principal character \(χ\) modulo \(q\), we construct an explicit Appell--Mellin generating function \(A_χ(t)\) whose associated Appell sequence satisfies \(R_n^χ(x) = L(-n,χ,x)\), and we prove the functional equation \(A_χ(t) = χ(-1)A_χ(-t)\). We further establish five structural properties of the polynomials \(R_n^χ\): identification with generalized Bernoulli polynomials, a difference equation, an explicit formula, a Fourier expansion, and the trivial zeros of \(L(s,χ)\). To the best of our knowledge, these results do not appear in the literature.

papers.title: Higher rank elliptic sieve via CM endomorphisms
papers.summary: A theorem of Landau and Ramanujan states that almost all integers are not sums of two squares (when ordered by their absolute value). Equivalently, almost all integers are not norms from the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. In this paper, we prove a version of this norm result for elliptic curves $E$. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with complex multiplication, such that $K$ contains the endomorphism ring of $E$. For a fixed non-torsion point $P \in E(K)$ and an abelian extension $L/K$, we show that subject to a technical condition, the $y$-coordinate of almost all multiples of $P$ does not belong to the norm group of $L$. The proof is an adaptation of an argument of Bhakta et al. , whose main tools are elliptic divisibility sequences and a sieve technique known as the elliptic sieve. To account for the points in $E(K)$ arising from the additional endomorphisms, we apply the elliptic sieve to elliptic nets, a higher-rank generalisation of elliptic divisibility sequences. This approach demonstrates the possibility of applying the elliptic sieve to $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points on elliptic curves and the usefulness of elliptic nets to counting problems on elliptic curves.

papers.title: Reconstruction of graphs and surfaces from derived categories
papers.summary: A pair of topological spaces $X$ and $Y$ is a \emph{Fourier--Mukai (FM) pair} if there is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories of derived sheaves of abelian groups \[\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))\simeq \operatorname{Shv}(Y;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z)).\] An FM pair $(X,Y)$ is \emph{non-trivial} if $X$ and $Y$ are not homeomorphic. We consider the question of whether non-trivial FM pairs $(X,Y)$ exist for which $X$ and $Y$ are both "nice" spaces, which in this article means admitting a triangulation. We show that the answer is no if $X$ is second-countable and either (i) one-dimensional, (ii) a surface, or (iii) the 3-sphere. In order to prove this, we define two invariants of dualizable categories. The first invariant is an extension of \emph{Tate--Hochschild cohomology} (aka singular Hochschild cohomology) to a class of dualizable categories satisfying a countability assumption. For a homology manifold $X$, we relate the Tate--Hochschild cohomology of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(\mathbb Z))$ to the homology at infinity of $X$ (in the sense of proper homotopy theory). The second invariant takes the form of a subcategory $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{Gor}}\subseteq\mathcal D$ called the \emph{Gorenstein locus}, defined for every dualizable stable category $\mathcal D$. For a triangularizable space $X$ and a field $k$, we show that the Gorenstein locus of $\operatorname{Shv}(X;\mathrm D(k))$ is equal to the full subcategory of sheaves supported on the $k$-homology manifold locus of $X$.

papers.title: Kuranishi spaces in a category of fibrant objects and their homotopy fiber products
papers.summary: We study several fundamental properties of the category $\mathbf{Kur}$ introduced in \cite{Kim1}. By defining fibrations and weak equivalences, we show that morphisms with manifold targets admit homotopy fiber products; this is then applied to obtain a notion of generalized intersections of two submanifolds. A definition of the Weinstein category in the context of Kuranishi spaces is also presented. Finally, we establish that $\mathbf{Kur}$ forms a category of fibrant objects in the sense of Brown \cite{Brown}, and discuss its homotopy category $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathbf{Kur})$.

papers.title: Schubert compactifications of matrix pencils
papers.summary: The Schubert compactification of a linear space of matrices $L \subseteq \textrm{Mat}_{n\times m}$ is a natural compactification of $L$ in the Grassmannian $\textrm{Gr}(n, n+m)$. This construction generalises classical Schubert varieties and matroid Schubert varieties, and it turns invariants of linear matrix spaces into projective and intersection-theoretic invariants of the associated variety. We develop this geometry completely in the case of matrix pencils, that is $\dim L=2$. The resulting Schubert surfaces are singular analogues of rational surfaces obtained as blow-ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$. We show that they are normal with quotient singularities, compute their degree, cohomology ring, and describe the distinguished rational curves and their intersection pairing in terms of the Kronecker invariants of the matrix pencil. Remarkably, this dictionary can be reversed: the invariants of the pencil are read off from intersection numbers and other invariants of the variety. In particular, we prove that the Schubert surface determines the regular component of the pencil, up to the natural action of $\mathrm{GL}_2 \times \mathrm{GL}_n \times\mathrm{GL}_m$. Finally, we prove that the ideal of Schubert surfaces of matrix pencils in the Plücker embedding is generated in degree $2$ and satisfies Green's property $N_p$ in a certain range.

papers.title: Genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields
papers.summary: We define genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields of odd characteristic. We express each as a product of two quadratic $L$-functions and explicit local factors at primes dividing the conductor, with a possible shift of the variable in one of the two quadratic $L$-functions. This product formula yields meromorphic continuation and functional equations. In the real case, we evaluate special values in terms of continued fractions and derive formulas for the product of class numbers of two imaginary quadratic function fields. These formulas are function field analogues of the Kaneko-Mizuno-Zagier formula.

papers.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
papers.summary: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = τ+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $τ= -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.

papers.title: On the existence of Gorenstein injective covers
papers.summary: For a locally finitely generated Grothendieck category, we characterise the Gorenstein injective covering property by several equivalent conditions, including closure under coproducts. To complete this characterisation, we construct a countable commutative Noetherian Cohen--Macaulay local ring of dimension one for which this property fails, answering negatively Iacob's question Question 1 whether character modules of Gorenstein injective modules over left Noetherian rings are Gorenstein flat. Using this characterisation, we prove that for Noetherian schemes the covering property is Zariski-local. Moreover, assuming that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathrm{QCoh}(X))$ is a covering class, we establish compatible adjunctions and recollements for homotopy categories of injectives and totally acyclic injective complexes under open restriction. However, this property is not stalk-local: we construct a commutative Noetherian ring $S$ such that $\mathcal{GI}(S_{\mathfrak{p}})$ forms a covering class for all prime ideals $\mathfrak{p}$, but $\mathcal{GI}(S)$ do not form a covering class.

papers.title: Weighted, GIT and Néron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
papers.summary: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the Néron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted Néron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the Néron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.

papers.title: Special Loci in the Moduli of Curves
papers.summary: We introduce new techniques to study mixed-characteristic special loci in moduli spaces and give several applications, focusing in particular on the moduli space $\mathsf{M}_g$ of curves. These applications include Zariski density results for split Jacobians, non-density results for supersingular loci, and lifting results for algebraic cycles, all under appropriate numerical conditions. Our methods generalize to more-or-less arbitrary moduli spaces mapping to Hodge-type Shimura varieties (and even some settings beyond the Shimura case), and relate to questions raised by Oort and de Jong.

papers.title: Zero-cycles and Brauer groups on certain Enriques surfaces
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the Chow group of zero-cycles $\text{CH}_0(S)$ for certain Enriques quotients $S$ of the Kummer surface associated to the product of two geometrically non-isogenous elliptic curves $E_1$ and $E_2$. We show that over fields of characteristic different from $2$ or $3$, the degree-zero subgroup $A_0(S) \subset \text{CH}_0(S)$ is 16-torsion. Over p-adic fields, we compute the transcendental Brauer group $\text{Br}(S)/\text{Br}_1(S)$. Using the Brauer-Manin pairing, we construct examples of Enriques surfaces for which $A_0(S)$ attains nontrivial 2-torsion elements arising from push-forward from the abelian surface $E_1\times E_2$.

papers.title: p-adic Hodge theory of unipotent completions revisited
papers.summary: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension, and let $X/K$ be an algebraic variety. We present a new proof that the unipotent completion of the étale fundamental group of $X_{\bar{K}}$ is a pro-de Rham representation, and show that it is pro-semi-stable whenever $X$ has semi-stable étale cohomology. We also reprove, using syntomic methods, that it is pro-crystalline at integral base points whenever $X$ admits a smooth proper formal model. All three proofs use the bar construction and are inspired by Wojtkowiak's approach to unipotent fundamental groups.

papers.title: Dolbeault Cohomology Growth under Curvature Rank Bounds
papers.summary: Let $L$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$, and let $r$ be the maximal rank of its curvature. We prove that $h^q(X,L^p\otimes E)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every fixed holomorphic vector bundle $E$, every $\varepsilon>0$, and every degree $q$. No positivity, constant-rank, or Kähler assumption is imposed. Consequently, the Kodaira--Iitaka dimension satisfies $κ(L|_{X_0})\le r$ on every connected component $X_0$ of $X$. The proof retains rank identities in finite Taylor jets under successive rescalings and factors bounded Hermitian kernels without a positive lower bound on the absolute values of the nonzero curvature eigenvalues. Exact Dolbeault restriction identities yield finite-rank approximations with additive rank bounds, which control cohomology.

papers.title: Gamma conjecture II and explicit Stokes data for a quadric projective bundle
papers.summary: We study the connection problem for the quantum differential equation of the Fano fourfold $X=\PP_{Q^3}(\OO\oplus\OO(1))$. The problem is to identify its canonical asymptotic solutions with exceptional objects and compute the associated Stokes data. We use exact Mellin--Bessel integral representations and uniform vector asymptotics on sectors wider than $π$, followed by analytic continuation that preserves the Gamma framing. Cohomological chiral symmetry and mutations of exceptional collections put all eight sections at a common phase. This proves Gamma conjecture II for $X$ and determines a full exceptional collection and its Stokes and central connection matrices at the unit Novikov point and a specified admissible phase. The chiral symmetry also gives a flat symmetric bilinear pairing, an orthogonality identity for the Stokes matrix, and an integral unipotent square root of the monodromy matrix for a full turn. We obtain explicit formulas for the connection data at the opposite phase; on the Gamma lattice, the half-turn acts by tensoring with a square root of the anticanonical bundle. The same spinor integral transform constructs two canonical Gamma sections for $\PP_{Q^{2m+1}}(\OO\oplus\OO(1))$, $m\geq1$, at positive parameters with distinct spectrum. Their sectors have opening greater than $π$, and their leading constants are independent of the dimension.

papers.title: Semifree Cochain Models for Fibrations Revisited
papers.summary: We construct cochain models for Serre fibrations over path-connected bases with coefficients in an arbitrary field. Our construction refines Brown's twisted tensor product to produce a differential graded module model over the singular cochain algebra of the base. If the homology of the fibre is finite dimensional in each degree and on which the action of the fundamental group of the base is degreewise nilpotent, then this model is a semifree resolution generated by the cohomology of the fibre. This extends the classical construction for simply connected bases. As applications, we compare the resulting model with arbitrary semifree resolutions, showing that every such resolution recovers the cohomology of the fibre after base change to the basepoint, and obtain an explicit bound on the page at which an associated spectral sequence collapses.

papers.title: Automorphic symbols and automorphic \emph{L}-values of GL(2) over imaginary quadratic fields
papers.summary: We study non-vanishing modulo primes of critical values of $L$-functions over imaginary quadratic fields twisted by Coates--Wiles characters. For a parallel weight two Hecke eigenform over an imaginary quadratic field, we prove that a positive proportion of Coates--Wiles characters have nonzero integral $L$-values modulo each prime in a positive-density set. The argument constructs automorphic symbols in parabolic homology with integral coefficients and expresses the critical values through their pairings with parabolic cohomology classes. A vertical family of additive averages of these pairings recovers Fourier coefficients and force the module generated by symbols to have full rank. We transfer this full-rank property to non-vanishing modulo primes. This extends the homological strategy of Kim--Sun from classical modular curves to arithmetic orbifolds, while addressing the unit obstructions specific to the imaginary quadratic setting.

papers.title: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
papers.summary: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$π\mapsto I_π(f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $π$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.

papers.title: Separating components of real algebraic varieties by cohomological invariants

papers.title: The inf spectrum of moduli space
papers.summary: Given a surface of genus $g \geq 2$, its inf spectrum is the ordered multiset of inf lengths of curves on the surface, the infimum being over all hyperbolic metrics. The proof involves developing a number of tools including the process of "thickening" a surface and the notion of model surfaces. These tools may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Sharp Polynomial Upper Bounds for Anticanonical Volumes
papers.summary: For every positive integer $n$, we prove that there is a constant $C_n$, depending only on $n$, such that $Vol(-K_X) \leq C_n ε^{-(2^n-n-1)}$ whenever $X$ admits an $ε$-lc log Fano boundary. The exponent is optimal in every dimension at least two, even for toric Fano varieties of Picard number one. In particular, the optimal exponent for fourfolds is eleven. We also prove an anticanonical interpolation theorem with optimal exponent $2^n-1$. The proof combines signed discrepancy estimates under projection, finite morphisms to projective space, and the canonical bundle formula. A reduction to a base bounded independently of $ε$, followed by a volume estimate along a flag, yields the sharper volume exponent.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Polishchuk--Van den Bergh conjecture on curves
papers.summary: We construct effective finite group actions on smooth projective complex curves for which Conjecture A of Polishchuk and Van den Bergh fails. For every $h\geq1$, an explicit $S_3$ action on the smooth projective model of $y^2=t^{12h-5}+t$ has quotient of genus $h$ and exactly one ramification orbit, with inertia of order three. The fixed quotient for the three-cycle class consists of two points, but its derived category admits no $\C$-linear exact fully faithful embedding into the equivariant derived category. More generally, when the coarse quotient has positive genus, we prove that the maximum number of pairwise completely orthogonal exceptional objects is $\sum_i\lfloor e_i/2\rfloor$, where $e_i$ are the inertia orders. We also characterize conjugacy-class decompositions with embeddings linear over the coarse quotient: such a decomposition exists if and only if $|[g]\cap H_i|\leq\lfloor e_i/2\rfloor$ for every nonidentity conjugacy class and every branch inertia group $H_i$. The sufficiency proof uses coloured paths of type $A$ and derived reflection functors, and produces kernels on the natural fibre products. The known ordered curve decomposition still yields a decomposition indexed by the connected components of the fixed quotients.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Ambro--Kawamata effective non-vanishing conjecture
papers.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ or $p\neq3$. We construct a terminal projective 4-fold $X$ and an ample Cartier divisor $D$ such that \[ 3K_X\sim0,\qquad D-K_X\ \text{is ample},\qquad H^0(X,D)=0. \] In char 0 this disproves the Ambro--Kawamata effective non-vanishing conjecture. From this example we construct a smooth projective 4-fold $Y$ with a semiample and big Cartier divisor $D_Y$ such that $D_Y-K_Y$ is basepoint-free and big and $H^0(Y,D_Y)=0$. We also give geometric variants and a separate terminal order 5 Jacobian quotient.

papers.title: Classification of reductive monoids
papers.summary: We classify reductive monoids over arbitrary base schemes by descent from the split classification in arXiv:2607.00322. For a reductive group scheme $G$, we construct its sheaf of based root data, abstract Cartan torus, abstract Weyl group, and a scheme of Weyl cones. The last of these represents the functor of isomorphism classes of rigidified reductive monoids with unit group $G$. As applications, we deduce a criterion for the existence of monoids that are not groups, prove an extension theorem over normal integral bases, and construct the Vinberg monoids without a quasi-split hypothesis.

papers.title: Generalizing Green's Syzygy Theorems to Symmetric Products of Curves
papers.summary: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$, and let $T_{n,L}$ denote the tautological line bundle on its $n$-th symmetric product $C_n$. We prove effective vanishing criteria for Koszul cohomology $K_{p,q}(C_n,T_{n,B};T_{n,L})$, extending two classical theorems of Mark Green. The main ingredient is a weight-one vanishing theorem proved by induction on $n$, using a filtration of the kernel bundle of $T_{n,L}$ to reduce the required cohomological vanishings to lower symmetric products. As a consequence, when $g\geq1$ and $n\geq2$, $T_{n,L}$ satisfies property $(N_p)$ for $\mathrm{deg}(L)\geq(n+1)g+p$. This bound is sharp for elliptic symmetric squares and also gives evidence for a folklore conjecture on adjoint syzygies.

papers.title: Stieltjes constants for Hurwitz-type L-series attached to periodic arithmetic functions
papers.summary: We investigate generalized Stieltjes constants attached to Hurwitz-type Dirichlet series of the form $$ L(s, f, x)=\sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{f(n)}{(n+x)^s} $$ where $f$ is a periodic arithmetic function and $x\in\mathbb C\backslash\{0,-1,-2,\dots\}.$ We prove that these series admit meromorphic continuation to the whole complex plane, with at most a simple pole at $s=1$. We further derive functional equations satisfied by $L(s,f,x).$ Our main result gives an explicit formulas of the Stieltjes constants $γ_n(f, x)$ appearing in the Laurent expansion at $s=1$. In particular, we obtain explicit evaluations in the case of rational $x$. As an application, we derive explicit closed-form expressions for the first three generalized Stieltjes constants associated with nonprincipal real primitive odd Dirichlet characters arising from quadratic fields. These expressions are given in terms of the class number of the corresponding quadratic number field. These results extend and unify recent work of Blagouchine and others on generalized Stieltjes constants and Hurwitz-type $L$-functions.
